take_homes: Access is not use. A licence count says nothing about whether anyone trusts the tool with real work, so I should ask what job the person is trying to get done and what they use today.
Write the people plan as seriously as the technical one, with named owners. Unnamed roles mean it is not ready.
Start with one person and one conversation about how they do the job today. That conversation tells me what to build.

monday.move: Ask one of my HR business partners how they put together their weekly people-metrics summary today, and what would have to be true for them to use an agent-made one instead. I would build nothing before that.
monday.who: One HR business partner I trust
monday.when: Monday or Tuesday, in a 30-minute conversation
monday.stop_condition: If they say the current way works well enough and nothing I describe would change that, I drop the idea or choose a different job.
monday.blocker: Employee data in an AI tool needs the works council and the DPO, and I have not asked yet. I would use a fake data sample for the first test and raise it with the DPO this week.

misconception.why: The story says companies run on the human principle, and adoption depends on trust and ownership, not only capability. That makes 'which roles go first' look like the wrong first question. I still expect headcount to come up in the leadership meeting, and the module did not give me an answer to it.

one_line: A good, honest module about why rollouts fail, with real people questions in it. The repeated 'note on context' paragraphs are filler, and I would cut them.
